questions.explanation: Present perfect simple for a finished action with a present result.
questions.q: I've ___ my keys — I can't find them anywhere.

questions.explanation: 'All morning' with an action verb takes the present perfect continuous.
questions.q: She's very tired because she ___ all morning.

questions.explanation: 'How long' questions about an ongoing action use the present perfect continuous.
questions.q: How long ___ English?

questions.explanation: A completed accident with a present result takes the present perfect simple.
questions.q: He ___ his leg, so he can't walk to school.

questions.explanation: 'Be' is a stative verb, so it cannot take the continuous form.
questions.q: They've ___ married for ten years.

questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous asks about a recent activity with a visible result now.
questions.q: Look at your hands! What ___?

questions.explanation: 'Know' is stative, so use present perfect simple, not continuous.
options: I have been knowing him for years.
I am knowing him for ten years.
I have known him for ten years.
I have know him for ten years.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?

questions.explanation: Present perfect simple with a finished quantity: 'three emails'.
questions.q: I've ___ three emails this morning.

questions.explanation: A completed event with a present result takes the present perfect simple.
questions.q: They've ___ the match — the score is 3-0.

questions.explanation: The continuous form asks about a recent activity that explains the present situation.
questions.q: You look exhausted! ___ football?

questions.explanation: Experience with 'twice' takes the present perfect simple.
questions.q: I ___ this film twice — it's brilliant.

questions.explanation: Ongoing weather with 'since' takes the present perfect continuous.
questions.q: It's ___ since early morning.

questions.explanation: 'Just' for a recently completed action takes the present perfect simple.
options: She has just finished her essay.
She has been just finishing her essay.
She has just been finishing her essay.
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is correct?

questions.explanation: 'Have' is stative here, so use present perfect simple, not continuous.
questions.q: How long ___ your new car?

questions.explanation: 'Know' is stative, so use present perfect simple with 'since'.
questions.q: We ___ each other since primary school.

questions.explanation: A completed change with a present result takes the present perfect simple.
questions.q: Her English ___ a lot since she moved here.

questions.explanation: A finished action with a clear present result takes the present perfect simple.
questions.q: He ___ all the cake! There's none left.

questions.explanation: A recent activity explaining a present situation takes the present perfect continuous.
questions.q: Why are the kids so dirty? They ___ in the garden.

questions.explanation: 'Been lived' is wrong — the continuous form needs verb+ing: 'been living'.
questions.q: Which sentence is WRONG?

questions.explanation: A finished quantity ('ten pages') takes the present perfect simple.
questions.q: She ___ ten pages of her book today.
